방학.t: 방학 is only for students/schools; workers take 휴가.

반.ex: 우리 반에는 학생이 열다섯 명 있어요.
반.x: There are fifteen students in our class.
반.e: Two words: 'class' (우리 반 = our class) and 'half'.
반.t: 'Half' is common with time: 세 시 반 = 3:30. For 'class' meaning a lesson, use 수업 instead.

입학하다.m: to enter (a school), to be admitted
입학하다.x: My younger sibling started elementary school this year.
입학하다.t: Pronounced [이파카다]. School takes 에: 대학교에 입학하다.

가까이.forms: 가까이 오다 · 가까이 살다; 가까이에 (near, as a place)
가까이.ex: 우리 집 가까이에 큰 공원이 있어요.
가까이.x: There's a big park near my house.
가까이.t: Before an amount it means 'nearly': 두 시간 가까이 기다렸어요 = I waited nearly two hours.

살이 찌다.forms: 살이 쪘어요 (I've gained weight) · 살이 빠졌어요 (I've lost weight)
살이 찌다.m: to gain weight, to put on weight
살이 찌다.ex: 방학 동안 많이 먹어서 살이 쪘어요.
살이 찌다.x: I ate a lot over vacation and gained weight.
살이 찌다.t: Some Koreans casually say 살 쪘네! to friends, but as a learner it's safer not to comment on weight.

힘들다.ex: 회사 일이 많아서 요즘 정말 힘들어요.
힘들다.x: I have a lot of work these days, so things are really tough.
힘들다.e: 힘 (strength) + 들다 (to take, to be needed): 'takes a lot of strength.'
힘들다.t: 힘들다 is about effort or exhaustion; 어렵다 is about something being hard to understand or solve.

화가 나다.forms: 화가 났어요 (I'm angry) · 화가 많이 났어요 (I'm really angry)
화가 나다.m: to get angry, to be angry
화가 나다.ex: 동생이 말도 없이 제 옷을 입어서 화가 났어요.
화가 나다.x: My younger sibling wore my clothes without asking, so I got angry.
rel: to be in a bad mood

속상하다.x: I had a fight with my friend yesterday, so I'm really upset.
속상하다.e: Native 속 'inside, gut' + 'hurt': your insides feel wounded.

어린이.x: May 5th is Children's Day in Korea, so there's no school.
어린이.t: 어린이 is a bit formal, used on signs and holidays; in conversation 아이 or 애 is more common.

그저께.x: I met a friend and saw a movie the day before yesterday.
그저께.t: The short form 그제 is also common in speech.

적응.x: Adjusting to life in Korea was easier than I expected.

친하다.x: I'm very close with my classmates.
친하다.t: It's an adjective, so use N하고/과 친하다; 'to get close' is 친해지다.

차라리.forms: 차라리 -는 게 낫다 (would rather / might as well)
차라리.m: rather, would rather, might as well
차라리.ex: 이렇게 기다릴 바에는 차라리 걸어가는 게 나아요.
차라리.x: Rather than waiting like this, we might as well walk.
차라리.t: Choosing the lesser of two evils: 차라리 ... 낫다 means 'it'd be better to just ...'.

어쨌든.m: anyway, in any case, at any rate
어쨌든.ex: 길이 막혀서 늦었지만 어쨌든 도착해서 다행이에요.
어쨌든.x: Traffic made us late, but anyway, I'm glad we arrived.
어쨌든.e: Short for 어찌했든 'however it was done'.

패스트푸드.ex: 패스트푸드를 너무 자주 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
패스트푸드.x: Eating fast food too often isn't good for your health.
패스트푸드.e: From English 'fast food'; Korean has no f sound, so f becomes ㅍ.

상징하다.x: The white on the Korean flag symbolizes peace.

소설가.ex: 제 꿈은 유명한 소설가가 되는 거예요.
소설가.x: My dream is to become a famous novelist.

판타지.ex: 판타지 드라마라서 주인공이 시간 여행을 해요.
판타지.x: It's a fantasy drama, so the main character travels through time.
판타지.t: Popular mixes include 로맨스 판타지 'romance fantasy', often adapted from web novels and webtoons.

부처님.x: I went to the temple and made a wish to the Buddha.
부처님.e: 부처 'Buddha' + honorific -님; 부처 came from 'Buddha' via Chinese.
부처님.t: His birthday, the 8th day of the 4th lunar month, is a public holiday called 부처님오신날, when temples hang lotus lanterns.

유튜버.ex: 제 동생은 요리 유튜버가 되는 게 꿈이에요.
유튜버.x: My younger sibling's dream is to become a cooking YouTuber.
유튜버.t: Run a channel: 유튜브를 하다. A YouTuber with a big following is a 대형 유튜버, and one who deals with a topic is named after it: 먹방 유튜버, 여행 유튜버.

도대체.forms: 도대체 + question word: 도대체 왜 · 도대체 뭐 · 도대체 어디 · short: 대체
도대체.m: on earth, in the world (what/why on earth …?)
도대체.x: Why on earth didn't you answer the phone?
도대체.e: Originally 'on the whole, in general' (all + general outline); now used to stress a question.
도대체.t: Shows frustration or strong curiosity. In casual speech it's often shortened to 대체: 대체 왜?

폭력.ex: 어떤 이유가 있어도 폭력은 절대 안 돼요.
폭력.x: Whatever the reason, violence is never okay.
폭력.t: Pronounced [퐁녁]: ㄱ before ㄹ turns into [ㅇ] and ㄹ into [ㄴ] (nasalization).

결리다.m: to feel a stiff, stabbing pain, to have a crick (neck, shoulder, side)
결리다.ex: 자고 일어났더니 목이 결려서 고개를 못 돌리겠어요.
결리다.x: I woke up with a crick in my neck and can't turn my head.
결리다.e: Used for a sharp, stiff pain that hurts when you move or breathe — think 'a crick'.

입학시험.x: That school's entrance exam is really hard.
입학시험.t: Pronounced [이팍씨험] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

작곡.ex: 그 가수는 자기 노래의 작곡도 직접 해요.
작곡.x: That singer composes their own songs too.

징역.x: He was sentenced to two years in prison by the court.
징역.t: Pattern: 징역 + time + 을 선고받다 'to be sentenced to X in prison'.

아울러.m: in addition, at the same time, together with
아울러.ex: 참석해 주셔서 감사드리며, 아울러 건강을 기원합니다.
아울러.x: Thank you for attending, and I also wish you good health.
아울러.e: From the verb 아우르다 'to bring together'.

몰리다.m: to crowd, flock; to be driven (into a corner); to be accused (of)
몰리다.x: Since it was the weekend, lots of people flocked to the park.
몰리다.e: Passive of 몰다 'to drive, herd': people get herded into one place.

알차다.x: This trip was short but full of good things.
알차다.e: Built from 알 'kernel, grain' + 차다 'to be full' — packed with substance.
알차다.t: Common with time and content: 알찬 하루, 알찬 정보, 방학을 알차게 보내다.

코가 납작해지다.forms: 코가 납작해져요 · 코가 납작해졌어요 · 코를 납작하게 만들다
코가 납작해지다.m: to be humbled, to have one's pride crushed, to be taken down a peg
코가 납작해지다.ex: 자랑만 하던 그는 시합에서 져서 코가 납작해졌어요.
코가 납작해지다.x: He was always bragging, but losing the match took him down a peg.
코가 납작해지다.e: In Korean idioms the nose stands for pride, so a flattened nose means crushed pride.

과도기.x: Adolescence is the transition period from childhood to adulthood.
과도기.e: Literally 'a period of crossing over' from one stage to the next.

우편함.x: There's a maintenance fee bill in the mailbox.

겨루기.x: I sparred with a friend in class today.
겨루기.t: Taekwondo training has two main parts, 겨루기 (sparring) and 품새 (forms); Olympic taekwondo is 겨루기.

체감 온도.x: With the wind, they say it feels like minus ten.
체감 온도.e: 體感 'felt by the body' + 溫度 'temperature'.
체감 온도.t: Common in weather reports: 체감 온도가 영하 15도까지 떨어지다. 체감 also appears in 체감 물가 'how expensive prices feel'.

충동.ex: 충동을 참지 못하고 비싼 옷을 샀어요.
충동.x: I couldn't resist the impulse and bought expensive clothes.
충동.t: 충동구매 'impulse buying' is a very common compound.

각박하다.x: The world has become so cold-hearted these days.
각박하다.t: Classic phrase: 세상이 각박하다 'the world is a cold place'.

부단히.ex: 그는 꿈을 이루기 위해 부단히 노력했습니다.
부단히.x: He worked tirelessly to make his dream come true.
부단히.e: Literally 'never cut off': without a break.
부단히.t: Nearly a fixed phrase: 부단히 노력하다 'to make unceasing efforts'.

한계점.ex: 계속되는 야근에 직원들의 인내심이 한계점에 이르렀어요.
한계점.x: With the constant overtime, the employees' patience reached its breaking point.
한계점.e: Literally 'limit-boundary point' — the point you can't go past.

토론자.e: -자 = person who does it: 토론자, 창작자, 운전자.

변호인.ex: 피의자는 변호인의 도움을 받을 권리가 있습니다.
변호인.x: A suspect has the right to the assistance of counsel.
변호인.e: Literally 'a person who speaks to protect' someone.
변호인.t: 변호사 is the profession; 변호인 is the role of defending a particular client in a case.

채권자.ex: 채권자들이 회사에 빌려준 돈을 갚으라고 요구했습니다.
채권자.x: The creditors demanded that the company pay back the money they had lent.
채권자.e: Literally 'person with a right to a debt'; -자 = person: 채권자, 소비자.
채권자.t: Pronounced [채꿘자] with a tensed ㄱ; don't mix it up with 채무자 'debtor'.

통풍.ex: 통풍이 있으면 술과 고기를 줄이는 게 좋아요.
통풍.x: If you have gout, it's good to cut down on alcohol and meat.
통풍.e: Literally 'painful wind', an old traditional-medicine name for the disease.
통풍.t: Homonym warning: 통풍 (通風) also means 'ventilation', as in 통풍이 잘 되다.

괄목상대.m: remarkable progress; seeing someone in a new light
괄목상대.ex: 그의 한국어 실력이 1년 만에 괄목상대할 만큼 늘었어요.
괄목상대.x: His Korean improved remarkably in just one year.
괄목상대.e: Literally 'rubbing one's eyes to look again' at someone who has improved.
괄목상대.t: The news phrase 괄목할 만한 성장 'remarkable growth' uses just the first half.

허장성세.m: bluster, empty bravado, putting on a show of strength
허장성세.x: His confidence was nothing but empty bluster.
허장성세.e: Literally 'puffing up emptiness, inflating one's voice and power.'
허장성세.t: Often paired with 부리다: 허장성세를 부리다 means to bluster or put on airs.

다분히.ex: 그의 발언에는 다분히 정치적인 의도가 있어 보여요.
다분히.x: His remarks seem to have a largely political motive.

여론형성.x: The media play a big role in shaping public opinion.
여론형성.e: 여론 is 'public opinion', literally 'the crowd's discussion'.

몽롱하다.x: I took cold medicine, and now my head feels a bit hazy.
몽롱하다.e: Both syllables picture a dim, hazy moon.
몽롱하다.t: Pronounced [몽농하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.
